summary: Airborne and among the most contagious viral diseases known - secondary attack rate >=90% in susceptible household/institutional contacts. Prodrome of fever (up to 105F), malaise, cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, then pathognomonic Koplik spots, then maculopapular rash (~14 days post-exposure). 20% of US cases are hospitalized; ~1 encephalitis case and 2-3 deaths per 1,000 reported cases. No FDA-approved antiviral exists - management is supportive care only. Vitamin A is a supportive adjunct, not a treatment or vaccine substitute. Contagious 4 days before to 4 days after rash onset; isolate 4 days post-rash if immunocompetent, for duration of illness if immunocompromised (prolonged shedding). (CDC Clinical Overview of Measles)

blocking.says: The label carries WARNING: THROMBOSIS, with risk factors including advanced age, immobilisation, hypercoagulable states, prior thrombosis, oestrogen use and central vascular catheters.

The card's own cited CDC source says 400 mg/kg. There is no range and no 100 mg/kg figure. The low end of the card's range is a FOUR-FOLD UNDERDOSE. The source also sets a route split the card omits: IGIV above 30 kg, GamaSTAN below 30 kg and not indicated for adults.

blocking.claim: Antiviral therapy — none exists; no pipeline agent to list
blocking.says: The core negative is confirmed — no FDA-approved antiviral. But the card's own source has a ribavirin section: in vitro activity, used off-label in severe or immunocompromised disease, oral commercially available, IV only via FDA EIND. The absolute framing could lead a clinician to believe nothing off-label exists.

blocking.claim: ProQuad row lists no contraindications at all
blocking.says: The label contraindicates it in hypersensitivity, immunosuppression, moderate or severe febrile illness, active untreated tuberculosis and pregnancy. A live attenuated vaccine row omitting pregnancy and immunosuppression is harm-capable.

blocking.claim: M-M-R II contraindications omit active untreated tuberculosis
blocking.says: The label lists five contraindications including active untreated TB. The card also narrows hypersensitivity to neomycin; the label says any component.

blocking.claim: Vitamin A row omits the pregnancy warning
blocking.says: Immediately adjacent to the toxicity sentence the card did use: pregnant women should avoid high-dose vitamin A, which has been linked to severe birth defects. The card gives no teratogenicity warning on the only row where it matters.
